name: South Watut
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Fischer 1963 'Watut' (composite grammar sketch of the three Watut lgs), per Holzknecht 1989:22; Holzknecht 1989 (PL C-115, read via sealang) has SWT phonemes but NO stress statement

sources.citation: Hooley, Bruce A. 1976. Austronesian languages: Morobe Province. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 2 (PL C-39), 335-348. Canberra: ANU. hdl 1885/253002
sources.note: Classification and village lists only (Dangal, Maralango in the 'Lower Watut Sub-Family'); the words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur.

sources.citation: Carter, John, John Grummitt, Janell Masters and Brian Paris. 2014. A sociolinguistic survey of the Watut languages: South Watut [mcy], Middle Watut [mpl], and North Watut [una]. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2014-006. Dallas: SIL International. 87 pp.
sources.note: Sec. 2.5 (pp. 12-13) reproduces Holzknecht's phoneme charts in IPA and explicitly declines to analyse phonology ('we.. do not analyse our data in these areas'); App. C 170-item IPA wordlists for Dangal, Bubuparum and Wawas (South Watut) carry no stress marks. Silent on stress. Sec. 2.4 research history enumerates all prior work (Fischer 1963, Hooley 1965 ms, Hooley 1971, Ross 1988, Holzknecht 1989, Landweer & Reitmaier 1990).

sources.citation: Holzknecht, Susanne. 1989. The Markham languages of Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics C-115. Canberra: ANU. viii+228 pp. doi 10.15144/PL-C115
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL5026 .H64 1989
sources.note: Sec. 4.2.6 South Watut, printed pp. 53-54: Table 4.7 phoneme inventory + notes 1-5 (t/c, d/j not distinct in Kumwats; c~t, j free variation; r~l; /e/ in two loans only; prothetic a to keep CVC). No statement of stress placement. Only stress mentions anywhere in the book: folk-perceived dialect differences are 'intonation, stress, or speed of delivery' (ch. 3); Duwet note 11 on unstressed vowel sequences; ch. 6 remark that the SWT/NWT final glottal replacing PMK *-n arose 'through stress rules' (rule not stated).

sources.citation: Holzknecht, Susanne C. 1988. The Markham languages of Papua New Guinea: a history of the Austronesian languages of the Markham and Ramu Valleys. PhD thesis, Australian National University. hdl 1885/133945
sources.note: Sec. 4.2.6 South Watut (scan p. ~105-106): identical phoneme table and five notes as the 1989 book; nothing on stress. Ch. 4 intro promises 'full phonological statements.. at a later date'.

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of western Melanesia. PL C-98. Canberra: ANU. doi 10.15144/PL-C98
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201.R67 1988)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201 .R67 1988
sources.note: Dangal/Maralango (= South Watut) appear only in subgrouping lists, source table (data from Hooley 1971) and index; no synchronic stress statement for any Markham language.

sources.citation: Hooley, Bruce A. 1971. Austronesian languages of the Morobe District, Papua New Guinea. Oceanic Linguistics 10(2): 79-151.
sources.note: Survey with Dangal and Maralango (= South Watut) wordlists and transcription conventions; may carry stress marks or a general prosodic remark for the 'Adzera family'. Low probability but the only other published primary data.

Holzknecht, Susanne (collector). 1985-88. Markham languages fieldwork recordings, PARADISEC collection SH2 (incl. South Watut speakers recorded in/near Lae). doi 10.4225/72/5911e78b2c85e

sources.note: The only other first-hand linguistic treatment of the Watut languages: a composite German grammar sketch of the South/Middle/North groups (Holzknecht 1989:9, 54). A 'Lautlehre'/'Betonung' note there would be the only published stress statement for any Watut language; the earlier scan also named it as the unreachable source.

sources.citation: SIL PNG language resources page for mcy (pnglanguages.sil.org/resources/search/code/mcy)
sources.note: not reachable by automated download; the only Internet Archive copy (2025) is itself a 403. No evidence anywhere of an Organised Phonology Data sheet or other SIL description for South Watut (the 2014 survey was commissioned to decide whether to begin any program).
